_note: Recorded measurement, not a gate. Nothing in CI asserts on these timings; see benchmarks/README.md for how the numbers are to be read and why this host is not 'suitable hardware'.
specification: §86 (animated glyphs: 20 000 — CPU half), §56 (text, MVP tier), §92 (CPU time)
iteration: one iteration is one layoutText call per string in the corpus — a frame in which every string's content changed
rowNote: This is the layout half of §86's animated-glyph row. The drawing half stays blocked on a feature, not on hardware: §56's bitmap atlas cannot be addressed per glyph, so the shipped path cuts one Texture per glyph cell and issues a draw call each (§55 frame sub-rectangle, §65 batching). benchmarks/README.md's 'feature' entry for this row is unchanged.
animationNote: A glyph that only moves is laid out once — animating a node's transform never re-enters layoutText. These numbers are the worst case for the row (content changing every frame), not its normal case.
targetNote: §86 gives this row a count (20 000) and no rate; 60 Hz is this file's reading of the table's neighbouring rows, not a rate the specification states for this row.
corpusNote: Headline rows use 25-character label-sized strings; attribution rows hold the glyph count fixed at 20000 and vary the string length. No corpus contains a space or a newline, so drawn glyphs equal characters exactly — asserted per row against quads.length.
allocationNote: layoutText allocates and Object.freeze's one TextQuad per drawn glyph, plus a frozen array and a frozen result per call: at 20 000 glyphs, 20 000 frozen objects per frame. Unlike §7b's math types this path is not allocation-free, and it is not required to be — the quads are the return value.
atlasBuildNote: buildGlyphAtlas() on the built-in 6 × 12 face, 128 × 128 texels, 95 covered characters. One-off setup, deliberately excluded from every throughput number.
attributionNote: The same 20000 glyphs laid out as 20000 × 1, 2500 × 8, 800 × 25, 100 × 200 characters. The glyph term is identical across the rows, so their spread is the per-call cost.
modelResidualNote: Largest relative deviation of `calls · perCall + glyphs · perGlyph` from the measured attribution rows. The two terms are fitted from the two extreme rows only, so this is how far the model misses the rows it did not see — published so the split is read as a description of the data, not a claim about it.

freezeControl.what: plain object literals with a TextQuad's eight numeric fields, each Object.freeze'd, collected into one frozen array — no engine code

freezeControlNote: An upper bound on the allocate-and-freeze share of a glyph, measured on plain object literals in this file rather than on engine code. The control writes constants where layoutText computes eight coordinates, so the true share is below it.
hostCaveat: CI container, no GPU, shared host; run-to-run spread is tens of percent. §86's 'suitable modern desktop hardware' is not this machine, so nothing here is a §86 verdict — and this row's drawing half is not measured at all.
